reasons: F07: the filing includes a restatement of prior-period financial statements, which is direct evidence that previously issued statements were materially misstated.
F01, F02: there is a material weakness in the financial close/reporting process, so the controls over producing these statements are not reliable.
F03: no auditor ICFR attestation is required (smaller filer), so management's controls get less outside scrutiny.
F04, F21, R16, R07: going-concern doubt, rising leverage and reliance on capital raising/securities issuance add financing pressure and give management an incentive to present better results.
F05: the auditor changed within two years, which together with the restatement and the weakness points to instability in reporting oversight.

R02, R04, R06, R15, F27: sales are falling, gross margin is falling sharply, SG&A is growing faster than sales, ROA is falling and inventory was written down. This is a weakening business where inventory and asset values are exposed to judgment.
R19: operating cash flow is well below net income (<0.8x), so reported earnings are not backed by cash. R08 (negative accruals) partly offsets this.
F24, F28: the critical audit matters include goodwill/intangibles and the segment reporting changed, both areas where impairment and judgment can be managed.

R09, R17, R03, F11, F16-F19: the M-score and F-score are below their thresholds, asset quality is normal, and there are no material related-party transactions, investigations, litigation or covenant problems, which lowers the risk somewhat.
